text: SQL Injection (SQLi) is a vulnerability that occurs when user input is directly included inside a database query without proper validation or parameterization. An attacker can inject SQL syntax to alter the structure of the query executed by the database.

code:
id | username | password
1  | admin    | admin123
2  | john     | qwerty
3  | alice    | 123123

text: Typical SQL Query in Web Applications

code: SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = 'admin' AND password = 'admin123';

id | username | password
1  | admin    | admin123

text: If a row matches both username and password conditions, the application treats the user as authenticated.

code: const query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='" + username + "' AND password='" + password + "'";

text: The application directly concatenates user input into the SQL query. This allows attackers to inject SQL syntax and change the logic of the query.

code: admin' --

text: The single quote terminates the string. The comment operator <highlight>(--)</highlight> disables the rest of the query.

code: SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='admin' -- ' AND password='anything';

Login successful
Welcome admin

text: Because the password condition is commented out, the database only checks <highlight>username='admin'</highlight>. The attacker logs in without knowing the password.

code: SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='' OR 1=1 -- ' AND password='';

id | username | password
1  | admin    | admin123
2  | john     | qwerty
3  | alice    | 123123

text: The condition <highlight>OR 1=1</highlight> always evaluates to true, so the database returns every row in the table.

code: SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='admin' -- ' AND password='anything';

Database ignores everything after --
Only condition checked: username='admin'
Result: admin row returned

text: SQL Injection happens when developers construct queries using string concatenation instead of safe query mechanisms such as prepared statements.

code: const query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=? AND password=?";

text: SQL Injection allows attackers to manipulate database queries by injecting SQL syntax through application inputs. This can lead to authentication bypass, database enumeration, and sensitive data extraction.
